scope: Bounded decoded-audio impairment recovery observation in Python and JavaScript. No transport/controller change, no A/V marker calibration change, and no retrospective qualification.

failed_prior_attempt.interpretation: A single residual identified sample prematurely ended the old recovery exception before decoded attenuation. The records prove near-silence and later identified return, but do not prove decoder/PLC internals or outgoing source packet timing.

algorithm: Inspect the complete aftermath through the existing two-second burst recovery deadline, retaining every finite near-silence sample (0<=RMS<=.001).
Choose the first identified sample at or after burst end and strictly after the final attenuation in that aftermath. The chosen return must be within the original deadline.

Require an identified continuation witness at least the existing maximum sampling gap (200ms) after return, with all intervening samples identified. The witness may follow the deadline; the recovery instant may not.

Exempt only near-silence between the actual burst start and chosen return. Retain all-window bad count, excepted attenuation count, numeric attenuated samples, first positive, last attenuation, stable return, deadline and witness.
Require actual bounded, ordered, non-overlapping burst aftermaths, identified immediately preceding audio, and complete sampling coverage. Any bad sample beyond the deadline remains unexcepted.
design.explicit_strengthening: The previous blanket burst exception could hide an above-threshold wrong tone during a burst. Wrong/ambiguous above-threshold tone, nonfinite values and negative RMS now fail even inside a network-burst interval. This does not apply to or alter mute handling.
design.unchanged: Clean/mute verdicts; actual burst boundaries; RMS/frequency identity thresholds; two-second return limit; all coverage bounds; unique ordinal A/V calibration; paired count and80/120ms limits.
